happeningTypes.name: Present a specified high-control health recommendation
happeningTypes.description: Deliver a declared pressure/no-choice health-message script. Content, derogation, politeness and restoration wording must be specified; identity is not efficacy or permission.
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, ability to decline, truthful content, contextual ethics/legal review, privacy and debriefing required; coercive clinical/practitioner application not authorized.

happeningTypes.name: Set an action-feedback delay distribution in a bounded task
happeningTypes.description: Configure specified keypress-to-feedback timing and learning history. Does not itself imply agency change, real control loss or behavioral consequences.
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, ability to decline, truthful content, contextual ethics/legal review, privacy and debriefing required; coercive clinical/practitioner application not authorized.

happeningTypes.name: Instruct imagining another person's perspective using available information
happeningTypes.description: Ask a consenting participant to imagine another's viewpoint using currently available information. Not conversation, new information provision, capacity training package or efficacy promise.
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, ability to decline, truthful content, contextual ethics/legal review, privacy and debriefing required; coercive clinical/practitioner application not authorized.

assertions.scope: Specified high-control health-message scripts in US college flossing/drinking and Slovenian masking/activity contexts; no general coercion or actual mandate scope.
assertions.measurement: Immediate four-item perceived freedom/choice threat; exact script bundle and comparison retained.
assertions.timing: Immediate task appraisal; persistence/generalization not established.
assertions.mechanism: Pressure/no-choice content can elicit perceived restriction, but social-value threat and other script features may contribute.
assertions.risk: Specific populations, bundled manipulations and construct/proxy limits; no practitioner permission, behavioral benefit or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Bounded specified messages alter directly measured perceived freedom threat; heterogeneous and alternative-mechanism evidence retained. No claim of independently mediated threat→reactance→behavior.

assertions.scope: Bounded keypress/feedback task with explicit learned delay distribution and0–250ms conditions.
assertions.measurement: Explicit agency ratings, not implicit timing alone, legal responsibility or real control.
assertions.timing: Immediate task appraisal; persistence/generalization not established.
assertions.mechanism: Temporal prediction/action-effect attribution can depend on learned delay distribution.
assertions.risk: Specific populations, bundled manipulations and construct/proxy limits; no practitioner permission, behavioral benefit or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Positive/negative task findings retained, but exact broad construct, protocol and transfer remain insufficient. Unknown is not zero.

assertions.scope: Imagining another's perspective using existing information, not conversation or multi-session training.
assertions.measurement: Interpersonal accuracy/confidence is not general perspective-taking capacity.
assertions.timing: Immediate task appraisal; persistence/generalization not established.
assertions.mechanism: Instruction may direct effort without supplying missing information or establishing skill change.
assertions.risk: Specific populations, bundled manipulations and construct/proxy limits; no practitioner permission, behavioral benefit or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Positive/negative task findings retained, but exact broad construct, protocol and transfer remain insufficient. Unknown is not zero.

findings.design: Two controlled message experiments; booklets intermingled, explicit random sequence not described
findings.timing: Immediate; threat check after negative cognition/anger measures
findings.result: Higher-control scripts increased measured freedom threat in both topics. Script wording also changes derogation/content; not isolated one-word or independently randomized latent state.
findings.limitations: Exact specified message package and immediate subjective appraisal only; assignment method ambiguity, convenience samples and bundled contrasts; no causal mediator or universal behavior benefit.

findings.population: Slovenian participants; masking and physical activity
findings.context: Slovenian participants; masking and physical activity
findings.measurement: Four-item freedom threat; separate anger/cognition and attitudes/intentions
findings.result: Perceived freedom threat higher for high-control messages in both topics. Downstream attitudes/intention nondetection in high-trust COVID group despite reactance, not automatic advocacy effect.
findings.limitations: Bundle not pure lexical control. Science trust measured and dichotomized, not randomized exact PSY-113 moderator; no calibration or universal effect.

findings.measurement: Perceived threat, reactance and persuasion associations
findings.result: Threatening language generally related to increased freedom threat/reactance; variation by study/sample and persuasion link not independent state-level causal identification.
findings.limitations: Review-primary overlap; heterogeneous messages/measures and coded moderators, no universal monotonic psychological path.

findings.design: Two message experiments with alternative predictive-model comparison
findings.result: Social-value threat provided stronger predictive account than freedom threat in reported analyses; partial suppression complicates unique freedom attribution.
findings.limitations: Alternative predictor comparison not independent causal-mediator intervention; threatens unique mechanism claim, not proof high-control messages never alter freedom appraisal.

findings.design: Meta-analysis of high-control language and gain/loss framing contrasts
findings.result: Gain/loss contrasts did not detect systematic differences in these outcomes; high-control language findings differ. Composite reactance operationalization includes anger/negative cognition.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE exact high-control operation/PSY-108 direct effect; no equivalence margin or supported zero. Studies overlap Ma/Dillard and effect counts are not independent studies.

findings.design: Experimental action-feedback timing and frequency manipulation
findings.timing: Immediate after feedback; learned distribution precedes ratings
findings.result: Mostly250ms experience can make longer delays receive higher agency ratings; universal short-delay increase is contradicted by learning-context reversal.
findings.limitations: Scoped task ratings, not general real-world agency; exact task/sample and state timing extraction incomplete. Retain context dependence, UNKNOWN overall direction.

findings.design: Cross-measure association within experimental task study
findings.measurement: Intentional binding, sensory attenuation and explicit agency
findings.result: Implicit effects replicated but between-person correlations between implicit and explicit measures, and between implicit measures, were not detected.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE exact delay intervention effect; null cross-measure association not proof within-trial independence or invalidity of all agency measures.

findings.measurement: Four distinct agency concepts and measures
findings.result: Operational mismatch and pooling can mislead interpretation; within/between-person timing relations may differ.
findings.limitations: Not empirical causal evidence or latent-state estimate; constrains construct transfer, not a numerical effect.

findings.measurement: Accuracy of other-person judgments and confidence
findings.result: No consistent accuracy benefit; some reductions and increased confidence. These results challenge assumed efficacy, but accuracy is not broad latent capacity.
findings.limitations: Outcome/task mismatch: neither nondetection nor occasional poorer accuracy proves no capacity effect. Sample/task transfer and exact measure need reconciliation.

findings.design: Conversation comparison experiment in same article
findings.result: Obtaining another's perspective through conversation improved accuracy in the final experiment.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE retained imagining-only identity; information acquisition not capacity increase, component/package inference prohibited.

findings.result: Training literature has varied definitions/measures, protocol fidelity, geography and social-validity limitations.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE single instruction identity; heterogeneous packages cannot establish broad capacity efficacy or a common dose.
